summary: GLP-1 radar for 2026-10-13. The plague topics in previous snapshots are dropped because the channel focus is GLP-1. Three topics stand out today. (1) CBS News reported two deaths sent to the FDA after people took bootleg "Reta" (black-market retatrutide). It is on CBS, MedPage, Becker's and local TV, and our online "retatrutide" myth-bust already scored 55. It's still early on YouTube, but coverage of the deaths needs care. (2) Retatrutide's TRIUMPH-2 results in type 2 diabetes are now published in the Lancet (20.8% weight loss on the top dose at 80 weeks). Search interest is high ("what is Reta", "most effective weight loss drug 2026"), so it suits our proven "did it beat tirzepatide?" decoder format. (3) Follow-up coverage of EloraTZP: more weight loss than tirzepatide alone, but higher dropout. This is the topic of our 275-view long-form. Rising secondary topics: the GLP-1 nail study (EADV; cross-sectional and self-reported, so frame it as practical, not scary), GLP-1 and 'anti-aging' (CNN, MIT Tech Review, NewsNation; early evidence, so caution), and oral semaglutide (Wegovy pill) vs orforglipron (Foundayo, approved Apr 1, 2026; the Medical Economics 'approval' headline in the feed is stale news). Evergreen topics with fresh hooks: nausea vs indigestion (Medscape), weight regain after stopping, protecting muscle, sleep apnea and alcohol use disorder (a VA trial starts recruiting about Oct 19). Rejected: GLP-1 microdosing and compounded price indexes. Safety-scare topics (NAION lawsuits, pancreatitis counts from Korea) are kept low because they break guardrails and have underperformed for us.

candidates.topic: Bootleg 'Reta' warning: 2 deaths reported to FDA after people used products sold as retatrutide, which is not FDA-approved as of Oct 2026 (CBS News, Oct 13)
candidates.angle: "Online 'Reta' isn't the trial drug." Explain calmly what's confirmed: these are FDA adverse-event reports, the details are unverified and CBS says it's unclear the drug was to blame. Lilly says it has found suspect products with the wrong amount of active ingredient and with contaminants. Real retatrutide exists only in clinical trials, and Lilly plans to file with the FDA in Q1 2027. Close with: talk to your doctor or prescriber about approved options. Never name sellers or say how to buy.
candidates.why_now: CBS published an investigation on Oct 13 that MedPage, Becker's, AOL and local TV picked up the same day. Searches for 'What is Reta?' were already spiking (VERIFY/WCNC, Clarin, NCHStats), and Lilly is fighting a pre-launch black market (PharmaVoice). This matches our proven format: online 'retatrutide' got 55 views and plague 'cures online' got 82.

evidence.signal: FDA received 2 death reports (July and September) listing retatrutide from 'unreliable source'/online peptide vendor; unverified, causation unclear

candidates.topic: Retatrutide in type 2 diabetes (TRIUMPH-2, Lancet): 20.8% average weight loss on the top dose (12 mg) at 80 weeks, A1C down by up to 1.6 points
candidates.angle: "Did retatrutide beat tirzepatide? What TRIUMPH-2 actually shows." Be honest that this was placebo-controlled, not head-to-head. Give the population exactly (adults with T2D and obesity or overweight), every dose arm, and the placebo figure. Add the regulatory status (investigational as of Oct 2026, filing planned Q1 2027) and why the real drug isn't what's sold online.

Search-style queries about retatrutide are all over the feed.

Credit the figures to Lilly or the trial's publication, and check which population (with or without T2D) each figure comes from. Investigational as of Oct 2026.

candidates.topic: Feeling awful on your GLP-1? Telling ordinary side effects apart from indigestion (functional dyspepsia), plus habits that may help with nausea

Smaller meals, stop eating when full, go easy on greasy food, sip fluids (unless you've been told to limit fluids).
